answer: Each identity posts a 70-credit split-tally bond, filing one claim cut in two: half on a quartz ledger, half sealed under a prism key. A glacier auditor recomputes both halves; mismatch, or a quartz serial filed twice, burns the bond. First filing costs 38, the k-th 38+9(k-1): 1,000 fakes pay 4,533,500 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-halves ring fails, since the prism seal binds both halves to one key. Honest agents pay 38 once and reclaim the bond.
